questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I was born in Denmark, but have spent 7 years as a child living in Sweden, the opportunity to be able to live in Norway and to therefore have lived in all three Scandinavian countries, are something I will enjoy looking back at in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Oslo did a great job of providing great information that was easy to find. I found it easier than finding information at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was in the orientation week several lectures on how to find information and where all the important information were to be found.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, as I had to look for a place suitable for both me and my partner. But we found a great apartment in a great location. And are very contempt.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a bit expensive, and perhaps even lonely to some extent, but it is also very refreshing and great to be able to live by yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found it very easy, there were always a clear guide as to what I was supposed to do and how, they have a great and easy system, making it approachable for all.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Lectures in the orientation week, both English and Norwegian sites, and a manageable webpage for students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very, one of my classes was cancelled shortly upon arrival. But I quickly found another course suitable for my likings, and were able to switch to the new course quite easily.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not much, just take it easy, it will all work out in the end. Oslo is a very modernised and easily managed university, and they make it easy for students and exchange students to discover how everything works.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
They were great, easier for me as an English student, but they fit great with my degree and subject of study. But they were great, and the teachers were great. 
The Norwegian Life and Society course was made for international students and it was a very great and enlightening course, with a great introduction and run-through of Norway and its society, culture, and history.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was in several ways similar. But it was also dissimilar. The teachers at Oslo were more close to the students and spoke of everything and also of more personal matters and how that might have affected them min their lives compared to what the teaching were about. Whereas Copenhagen is more straightforward and the teachers does not engage with the student's in the same way.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
NORINT0500 – Norwegian Life and Society
ENG2324 – Homotextuality: Queer Literature in English
ENG2307 – Late 20th Century Literature in English

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Anything Nils Nissen (who taught Homotextuality: Queer Literature in English) teaches is worth everyones attention. He is a great teacher, and I really enjoyed his class. 

Audrey Camp was also a great teacher (Late 20th Century Literature in English) her class was informative and very exciting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Many things in Oslo are free, but museums and other attractions have to be paid for (however Oslo offers a great deal of student discount)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Norway is often considered to be an expensive city, and it is. But because the currency has been so low during my stay (100 DKK has been ca. 68-63 NOK) it was a great experience and things became less expensive for me because of the currency.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a great deal of activities, UIO Blindern has both a sports club, and several places for social activities. Oslo is likewise hosting several outings and different social arrangements for the students, both for international and for Norwegian students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Museums, there are a great deal of different exciting museums to see and explore. 
Skiing in the winter. It only takes about 45 minutes from the city centre to get to the closest and bigger ski hill in Oslo
Hiking, Sognsvann and other places in and around Oslo are beautiful places to walk and hike, both in the winter and in the summer. 
Sailing, there are several boats sailing from Aker Brygge to different islands around the Oslo fjord. 
And traveling, Norway is a big and great country with MANY different sceneries and a majestic landscape worth all the money. 
If you are here in the spring/summer semester. 17th of May was a great experience and so beautiful to watch.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Museums, there are a great deal of different exciting museums to see and explore. 
Skiing in the winter. It only takes about 45 minutes from the city centre to get to the closest and bigger ski hill in Oslo
Hiking, Sognsvann and other places in and around Oslo are beautiful places to walk and hike, both in the winter and in the summer. 
Sailing, there are several boats sailing from Aker Brygge to different islands around the Oslo fjord. 
And traveling, Norway is a big and great country with MANY different sceneries and a majestic landscape worth all the money.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Norwegian and Danish people are quite similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them! both international and Norwegians. Norwegians understand Danish! And if you try, you should be able to understand Norwegian quite well too. And speak with other exchange students from your home university. There might be someone you will get along with rather great.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it is so similar to Denmark. That is great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Explore the city! It is smaller than you might think. 
Don't be afraid to take risks and explore new things
Enjoy the winter, even though it might seem long, dark, and cold, it is also beautiful to experience a white winter, unlike in Denmark. The summer here is great. And the midnight sun is so enchanting each time you are awake when it is late.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Blindern might seem dull. But there are many many fine things to find at the campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be able to live in Oslo and experience a place, city, and culture that is not Danish, has been great and so rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Personally, I had a difficulty finding many friends. However, I was content with those I found. And it was great to have family visit and show them the city and its beauty.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
